name: Mercedes-Benz 300 SL (W194)
description:
The car that brought Mercedes back after the war, and the first to be given gullwing doors — not for effect, but because the spaceframe carried its tubes so high through the flanks that a conventional door could not be cut into them.

Racing
In 1952 the W194 won outright at Le Mans, at Bern-Bremgarten, in the sportscar race of the Eifelrennen at the Nürburgring and in the Carrera Panamericana in Mexico. It took second and fourth at its first outing, the 1952 Mille Miglia, and won the Rally Stella Alpina in 1955, in the last edition of that event.

The results were surprising given the engine: carburettors only, 175 hp, less than the competing Ferraris and Jaguars and less even than the 300 SL road car that was developed from it and sold from 1954. Low weight and very low drag made up the difference over a long race.

It was that road car — the W198 gullwing coupé — that privateers took to the 1955 Mille Miglia in numbers, John Fitch winning the production class with one.
author: GeroDa74
